title: Code structure: a tests folder, coding standards, readable names and JSDoc

spec.summary: The code works, but it is harder to read and change than it should be. Unit tests sit beside the code in `src/` (30 files), so tests and code are mixed when browsing; there are no written coding standards; 34 % of the names declared in `src/` are one letter (5,593 of 16,459), 38 % of exported functions have no JSDoc (333 of 880), 19 files are over 600 lines (the largest 1,443) and 103 functions over 80 lines. 407 moves every test into a top-level `tests/` folder (unit, integration, e2e), writes the standards down (naming, JSDoc, SOLID as applied here, sizes, performance), makes ESLint enforce what it can, and brings the existing code up to them without changing what the app does. (Tests beside the code never reached the build: Vite bundles only what the app imports, and the Docker image and the desktop app ship only `dist/`; 407 keeps that proven by a check.) It comes before 207 so Phase 2’s remaining features are written to the standards from the start.

US-1.text: As the maintainer, I want all tests in one `tests/` folder, split into unit, integration and e2e, so that code and tests don’t mix and I can find any test quickly.

US-2.text: As a contributor (or an agent), I want written coding standards that the linter checks, so that new code is consistent without anyone having to remember the rules.

US-3.text: As someone reading the code, I want descriptive names and a JSDoc on every exported function, so that I understand a function without reading its body.

US-4.text: As the maintainer, I want large files split into modules that each do one job, so that a change touches one small place and is easy to review.

US-5.text: As a user, I want none of this to change how the app looks, behaves or performs, except where it gets faster.

AC-1.text: Every test lives under `tests/`: `tests/unit/` (one module, mirroring `src/`’s paths, e.g. `tests/unit/engine/keyframes.test.ts`), `tests/integration/` (several modules together: the stores, the decoder pool with its fake decoder, the preview sound), `tests/e2e/` (the Playwright tests, from `e2e/`) and `tests/support/` (shared fixtures and fakes, e.g. `timeline.testkit.ts`) (Q1). A check (in `npm run check`) fails if a `*.test.ts` or test helper appears under `src/`.

AC-2.text: After the move the same tests run and pass: `npm run test:unit` runs the same 1,672 unit and integration tests (more if 407 adds any), `npm run test:e2e` the same e2e tests; `npm run check`, the editor’s test explorer and single-test commands (documented in CLAUDE.md) work with the new paths.

AC-3.text: No test code reaches what is shipped: `scripts/check-bundle.mjs` (in `npm run build`) fails if any built file contains a module from `tests/` or test-only code (Vitest, the fakes); the Docker image and the desktop package keep shipping only `dist/` and the listed Electron files.

AC-4.text: `specs/coding-standards.md` says how code is written here, with a short example of each rule: names (descriptive; the one-letter exceptions of Q3), JSDoc (every exported function, class, React component and type: what it does, its parameters, what it returns, what it throws), SOLID as it applies to this codebase (Q7: one job per module, layers that only depend downwards, small interfaces), sizes (Q4), React (hooks, component size, props), performance (no allocation per frame in the drawing and decoding paths; measure before optimizing), errors (`logError`), comments, and tests (where they go, how they are named). The constitution’s Definition of Done and CLAUDE.md point to it.

AC-5.text: ESLint enforces the rules it can: name length (Q3’s exceptions only), JSDoc on exports (`eslint-plugin-jsdoc`, BSD-3-Clause, a development dependency only), function length and cognitive complexity (Q4, Q12), the React rules (AC-12), the type rules (AC-13), and the layers’ import direction (`data` → `engine` → `state` → `components`; `engine` never imports `state` or `components`). At the end of 407 `npm run lint` has 0 errors with every rule on as an error for `src/` and `electron/`.

AC-6.group: The existing code brought up to the standards
AC-6.text: No one-letter names are left in `src/` and `electron/` outside Q3’s exceptions (5,593 in `src/` on 2026-10-13), as the lint rule reports.

AC-7.group: The existing code brought up to the standards
AC-7.text: Every exported function, class, React component and type in `src/` and `electron/` has a JSDoc (333 exported functions without one on 2026-10-13), as the lint rule reports.

AC-8.group: The existing code brought up to the standards
AC-8.text: Modules that do more than one job are split by responsibility, each with one job and a short header saying what it is for: at least the 19 files over 600 lines on 2026-10-13 are reviewed and the mixed ones split (e.g. `engine/render.ts`, `state/video.ts`, `components/studio/Timeline.tsx`); every function meets Q4’s length and cognitive-complexity limits (103 functions over 80 lines on 2026-10-13). A file’s length alone is a review signal, not a rule (Q4); data files are exempt.

AC-9.text: Behaviour is unchanged: every unit, integration and e2e test, the self-test (~6,100 checks: every product × size × layout, print packs, agent tools) and the MCP test pass before and after; the 201–206 video fixtures export identical inputs and pixel-identical frames; the entry chunk is no larger than before (327 KB). These run at the end of 407 itself, not in 290 (Q9).

AC-10.text: A performance review of the hot paths (video frame drawing `renderStack` / `frameStack`, the decoder pool, the sound mix, the photo pipeline, the print renderer) is recorded in `specs/features/407-code-structure/` with measurements; a change is made only where it measures at least 10 % faster (Q8), with before / after numbers; no timing check gets slower.

AC-11.text: CLAUDE.md (commands, single tests, the layers), `specs/testing-strategy.md` (the new layout and what is unit / integration / e2e), `specs/architecture.md` and `specs/lld.md` (module paths after the splits), `specs/build.md` (scripts) and `memory/` describe the new structure; relative links resolve.

AC-12.text: The code follows the current React rules: every rule of `eslint-plugin-react-hooks` v7’s `recommended-latest` preset (the Rules of React that the React Compiler relies on: purity, immutability, refs, set-state in effects and render, static components, memoization) is an error and passes (27 findings in 16 files on 2026-10-13, today switched off); effects are used only to sync with things outside React (106 `useEffect` today, each one checked). Whether the React Compiler is then turned on is Q11.

AC-13.text: Types do the checking, not casts: typescript-eslint’s type-aware `strictTypeChecked` and `stylisticTypeChecked` presets pass; type assertions (`as`, 379 today, 13 of them `as unknown as`) and non-null assertions (`!`, 177 today) are replaced by narrowing, type guards or better types, and the few left carry a comment saying why; object shapes are named `interface`s (121 functions take inline object types today), with utility types (`Pick`, `Omit`, `Partial`, `Readonly` …) where they express a real relation instead of copies; `readonly` where data isn’t changed. Q13 decides which stricter compiler options come in 407.

Q1.text: The `tests/` layout? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-13):_ `tests/unit/` mirrors `src/` (one test file per module it tests); `tests/integration/` holds tests that drive several modules together (today: `state/*.test.ts`, `decodePool.test.ts` with its fake decoder, `previewSound.test.ts`); `tests/e2e/` takes `e2e/`; `tests/support/` the shared fixtures and fakes (`timeline.testkit.ts`, the fake decoder, the recording canvas). The roadmap dashboard’s own tests stay with that tool (`tools/`, a separate app) until Q6’s follow-up.

Q2.text: The in-app self-test (`src/dev/selftest.ts`, `videoChecks.ts`, `poolChecks.ts`, `playbackChecks.ts`, ~5,000 lines) runs inside the Electron app, in the page. Where does it go? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-13):_ `tests/selftest/`, loaded by `main.tsx` only in development builds (as today, behind `import.meta.env.DEV`), with AC-3’s check proving it never reaches the production build. `src/dev/showcase` and `printSamples` (development pages, not tests) stay in `src/dev/`.

Q3.text: Which one-letter names, if any, are allowed? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-13):_ only `_` for a value that is deliberately unused, and `x` / `y` for a point’s coordinates (they are the axes’ real names); everything else is descriptive: `index` not `i`, `clip` not `c`, `context` not `ctx` or `x`, `width` / `height` not `W` / `H`, `error` not `e`, `event` not `e`. The lint rule (`id-length` with these exceptions) applies to variables, parameters, functions and properties we declare.

Q4.text: Size limits: is a 500-line file limit needed? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-13):_ no hard file limit. Line count is only a proxy; what keeps code maintainable is one job per module (AC-8, Q7), short functions and low cognitive complexity. So: functions at most 80 lines and cognitive complexity at most 15 (errors); React components at most 250 lines (error); a file over 800 lines is a lint **warning** that asks for a review (split if it mixes jobs, keep if it is one cohesive job, e.g. one renderer). Data-only files (`src/data/`, `docs.ts`) and tests are exempt.

Q5.text: All at once or step by step? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-13):_ step by step, one folder per task, each its own commit with every test green, in this order: the tests move first (smallest risk, AC-1–AC-3), then the standards and lint rules as warnings (AC-4, AC-5), then `engine/`, `state/`, `agent/` + `ai/` + `lib/` + `platform/`, `components/`, `dev/` → `tests/selftest/`, `electron/`; each folder’s rules become errors when it is done. Estimated at 3–5 working days of tasks; Phase 2 work (207) waits for it.

Q6.text: Scope: what is cleaned up? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-13):_ the shipped code: `src/` and `electron/`. The development tools (`scripts/`, `tools/specs-index`, `tools/roadmap-dashboard`) follow the same standards for new code but are cleaned up later in their own feature (408), so 407 stays reviewable.

Q7.text: What does SOLID mean here, concretely? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-13):_ **S**: one job per module (e.g. `state/video.ts` becomes the store core and history, clip edits, keyframe actions, transition actions and export; `render.ts` and `Timeline.tsx` split the same way). **O**: products, sizes, layouts, kinds stay data-driven (add a table entry, not a branch), as `src/data/` already does. **L**: few classes here; where an interface has several implementations (frame sources, AI providers, file sinks) each honours it fully. **I**: small props and options interfaces, not one large shared one. **D**: layers depend downwards only (`data` → `engine` → `state` → `components`), enforced by lint; platform differences behind `platform/` and `lib/`. No class hierarchies added for their own sake.

Q8.text: How is “optimized” judged? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-13):_ by measurement, not by eye: the existing timing checks (preview frame time, export speed, the pool’s decode timings, the print renderer’s time per page) before and after; a change goes in only with at least 10 % gain on its path and no loss elsewhere. Readability changes (renames, splits) must not slow anything (checked by the same timings).

Q9.text: Heavy tests (D-033 puts them in a phase’s test pass)? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-13):_ 407 is not a phase feature and touches every file, so it runs the full Definition of Done itself at its end (e2e, self-test, MCP, licences, build) and after each large folder (components, dev), not deferred to 290.

Q10.text: Order with Phase 2? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-13):_ 407 first (branched from `main`, merged into `main` when done), then 207 branched from the updated `main`, written to the standards from its first line.

Q11.text: The React Compiler? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-13):_ yes, after AC-12, as the last step of 407: `babel-plugin-react-compiler` 1.0 (MIT, a build-time development dependency, nothing new shipped) through the Vite React plugin, for the whole app; then remove the manual `useMemo` / `useCallback` / `memo` it makes unnecessary (22 today). It is worth less here than in most apps (the heavy work is canvas drawing and decoding, outside React, and screens are already lazy-loaded), so it goes in only if the e2e and timing checks show no regression; the gain is mostly simpler components. If the plugin can’t be wired into this Vite version, it waits and AC-12 still applies.

Q12.text: Cognitive complexity (as SonarQube measures it)? The usual ESLint rule is in `eslint-plugin-sonarjs`, which is LGPL-3.0-only; our licence policy allows weak copyleft only with an approved exception (`specs/licensing.md`). (`eslint-plugin-cognitive-complexity` on npm is a security placeholder for a removed malicious package: never install it.) _Answer (accepted 2026-10-13):_ approve an exception for `eslint-plugin-sonarjs` as a **development-only lint tool**: never shipped, never bundled, not modified, so LGPL’s obligations (which apply when distributing it) don’t arise; recorded in `specs/licensing.md` and `memory/decisions.md`. It also brings Sonar’s other maintainability rules (duplicate strings, identical branches, nested ternaries). _Alternative:_ ESLint’s built-in `complexity` (cyclomatic, MIT) only, and SonarQube for IDE in the editor. The maintainer chose `eslint-plugin-sonarjs` (2026-10-13).

Q13.text: Stricter TypeScript compiler options? `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` (an array or record read may be undefined) catches real bugs but reports 1,400 errors today; `noImplicitReturns` and `noImplicitOverride` report 3. _Answer (accepted 2026-10-13):_ turn on `noImplicitReturns` and `noImplicitOverride` in 407; `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` folder by folder with the clean-up (it touches the same lines), on for the whole of `src/` by 407’s end. `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` waits (it changes how optional fields are written across the document gates).

changelog.text: Created: draft spec with 11 acceptance criteria and 10 open questions with proposed answers (the maintainer asked for a tests folder, coding standards, SOLID, JSDoc and no one-letter names before 207).

Second pass: no hard file-length limit (Q4: function length and cognitive complexity instead); AC-12 React rules, AC-13 types; Q11 React Compiler, Q12 cognitive complexity (sonarjs is LGPL), Q13 stricter compiler options; measured baselines.
Q1–Q13 accepted as proposed (Q12: `eslint-plugin-sonarjs` under a development-only LGPL exception; Q13 as proposed, D-037); Approved.
Plan written and approved with the spec (§1–§8, D1–D3, D-037).

sections.title: Non-Functional Requirements
sections.markdown:
- **Behaviour-neutral:** no change to what the app shows, saves, exports or how fast it is (except measured speed-ups, AC-10); every test green after every task (AC-9).
- **Reviewable:** one folder per task and commit; moves (`git mv`) separate from edits, so history follows the files.
- **Performance budgets kept:** code splitting stays as it is (screens and dialogs lazy-loaded, AI, Mediabunny and other heavy code behind dynamic `import()`; the entry chunk budget of 350 KB checked by `npm run build`, 327 KB today); splits must not pull code into the entry chunk.
- **Dependencies:** development only (`eslint-plugin-jsdoc` BSD-3-Clause; `babel-plugin-react-compiler` MIT if Q11; `eslint-plugin-sonarjs` LGPL-3.0 only with Q12’s exception), each in `scripts/check-licenses.mjs` as not shipped; nothing new in the shipped app.
- **Free and open source:** unchanged.

sections.title: Out of Scope
sections.markdown:
- New features or behaviour changes; UI changes.
- `scripts/` and `tools/` clean-up (408, Q6).
- A different test framework (Vitest and Playwright stay).
- Rewrites for style alone: a module is split or renamed to meet a standard, not redesigned.

risks.text: **Renames or splits change behaviour by mistake** (thousands of edits). Mitigation: the type checker, 1,672 unit tests and lint after every task; the full e2e and self-test after `components/` and `tests/selftest/` and at the close; small commits, one folder each, easy to bisect.

**Saved projects or agent tools change shape** if a persisted field is renamed. Mitigation: fields in documents (`toDocument`, `mergeProject`, `mergeLayers`, `mergeDesign`) and agent tool schemas keep their names (`id-length` doesn’t check properties); the document tests’ byte-identical round trips and the MCP test catch a slip.

**Type-aware lint is slow** on ~50,000 lines. Mitigation: measured when the rules land (§4); ESLint cache; if too slow, type-aware rules on changed files in `npm run check` and a full run at the close.

**A licence problem with the new development tools.** `eslint-plugin-sonarjs` is LGPL-3.0: approved as development-only (D-037), recorded in `specs/licensing.md`, never shipped; `oxc-transform-react` and `eslint-plugin-jsdoc` are MIT / BSD-3; versions pinned; `npm run check:licenses` unaffected (they aren’t shipped). Typosquats avoided (`eslint-plugin-cognitive-complexity` is a security placeholder).

**The React Compiler changes rendering** (Q11). Mitigation: it comes last, after the rules pass; diagnostics reviewed; e2e, self-test and timing compared; turned off with the reason if anything regresses.
**Size of the work** (~3–5 days, Phase 2 waits). Mitigation: tasks per folder, each mergeable on its own; the branch is merged into `main` when 407 closes, 207 starts from it.

sections.title: Approach
sections.markdown:
Behaviour-neutral throughout: every step is a move, a rename, a split or a type / lint fix, proven by the existing tests, and committed on its own with `npm run check` green. The order follows Q5: tests move first, then the standards and the lint rules (as warnings), then the code folder by folder (each folder's rules become errors when it is done), then the React Compiler and the performance review, with the full Definition of Done at the end (Q9).

**§1 Baselines (AC-9, AC-10).** Before anything moves: the unit test count (1,672), the e2e pass list, the self-test check count and result, `npm run test:mcp`, the export inputs of the 201–206 fixtures (the self-test's video checks compare them), the entry chunk (327 KB), and the timing numbers of the hot paths (§7). Plus a standards report (`scripts/standards-report.mjs`): per folder and rule, the lint findings and the `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` errors, so each task records its numbers going to 0.

**§2 Tests into `tests/` (AC-1–AC-3, Q1, Q2).** `git mv` only (history follows), then import fixes. `tests/unit/<src path>/x.test.ts` for one-module tests; `tests/integration/` for `state/*.test.ts`, `decodePool.test.ts`, `previewSound.test.ts`; `tests/support/` for `timeline.testkit.ts` and the fakes now inside test files (the fake decoder, the recording canvas, the fake audio element), shared instead of copied; `e2e/` → `tests/e2e/`; `src/dev/{selftest,videoChecks,poolChecks,playbackChecks}.ts` → `tests/selftest/`, loaded by `main.tsx` only in development (`import.meta.env.DEV`, as today). Tests import the app through a path alias, `@/` → `src/` (D1), set in `vite.config.ts` and the tsconfigs. Config: Vitest `include` the `tests/{unit,integration}` and `tools/` test globs; Playwright `testDir: 'tests/e2e'`; `tsconfig.tests.json` (referenced from `tsconfig.json`) type-checks `tests/`; `tsconfig.app.json` also includes `tests/selftest` (imported by the app in development). Guards: `scripts/check-structure.mjs` (in `npm run check`) fails on a test or test helper under `src/`, and on `src/` importing `tests/` other than `main.tsx`'s development import; a build-only Vite plugin fails `npm run build` if any chunk holds a module from `tests/` (AC-3).

**§3 The written standards (AC-4).** `specs/coding-standards.md`, each rule with a short good / bad example from this codebase: names (Q3; persisted document fields such as a keyframe's `t` / `v` or a box's `x` / `w` keep their names, since renaming them would change saved projects; code destructures them into descriptive names), JSDoc (what, `@param`, `@returns`, `@throws`; no types in JSDoc, TypeScript has them), SOLID as in Q7, sizes (Q4), cognitive complexity (Q12), React (AC-12: the Rules of React, effects only to sync with outside systems, components small, props interfaces named), types (AC-13: interfaces for object shapes, guards over casts, utility types for real relations, `readonly`), layers and imports, errors (`logError`), performance (no allocation per frame on the drawing and decoding paths; measure first), comments, tests (where, naming, one behaviour per `it`). The constitution's Definition of Done and CLAUDE.md link to it.

**§4 The lint and compiler rules (AC-5, AC-12, AC-13, Q4, Q12, Q13).** `eslint.config.js` gains: `id-length` (min 2; exceptions `_`, `x`, `y`; properties not checked, §3); `eslint-plugin-jsdoc` (`require-jsdoc` for exported functions, arrow functions, classes, interfaces and types; `require-param`, `require-returns`, `no-types`); `max-lines-per-function` 80 for `.ts` and 250 for `.tsx` (components), blank lines and comments not counted; `max-lines` 800 as a warning; `eslint-plugin-sonarjs` (recommended, `cognitive-complexity` 15); `eslint-plugin-react-hooks` `recommended-latest`; typescript-eslint `strictTypeChecked` + `stylisticTypeChecked` with `projectService` (type-aware), `consistent-type-definitions: interface`; the layers with core `no-restricted-imports` per folder (`src/data` imports nothing of the app; `src/engine` not `state` / `components`; `src/state` not `components`). Data files (`src/data/`) and tests are exempt from the size rules. Every new rule starts as a **warning**; a list of finished folders in the config turns them into errors there (§5). tsconfig: `noImplicitReturns` and `noImplicitOverride` on now (3 errors fixed); `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` tracked per folder by the standards report and turned on for `src/` when its count is 0 (Q13). `eslint-plugin-sonarjs` gets its development-only exception row in `specs/licensing.md` (D-037).

**§5 The clean-up, folder by folder (AC-6–AC-8, AC-12, AC-13).** In this order, each folder one or more tasks, each task one commit with `npm run check` and `npm run build` green: `engine/` (with its gpu subfolder), `state/`, `data/` + `lib/` + `platform/` + `agent/` + `ai/`, `components/` (studio, ig, then the rest), `tests/selftest/`, `electron/` (CommonJS: names, JSDoc, sizes; no type rules). In each: rename one-letter names to what they hold (`clip`, `index`, `context`, `width`, `event`), add JSDoc, fix casts and non-null assertions with guards and better types, fix the React findings, fix `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` errors, and split modules that mix jobs (known: `engine/render.ts`, `engine/timeline.ts` into tracks / sound plan / document gate, `engine/masks.ts`, `engine/layers.ts`, `state/video.ts` into store core and history / clip edits / keyframes / transitions / media and export, `components/studio/Timeline.tsx` into rows / track header / keyframe and cut marks / transport, `VideoWorkspace.tsx` and `PhotoWorkspace.tsx` into their panels, stage and inspector). Importers are updated to the new modules; no barrel files re-exporting old paths (D2). Then the folder's rules become errors. After `components/` and after `tests/selftest/`: the full e2e and self-test (Q9).

**§6 React Compiler (Q11).** After AC-12's rules pass everywhere: `react({ compiler: true })` in `vite.config.ts` with `oxc-transform-react` (MIT, the plugin's built-in, Rust port of the compiler; a development dependency, D3); `logDiagnostics` once to list components it skips, each fixed or noted. Then remove the manual `useMemo` / `useCallback` / `memo` it makes unnecessary (22). Kept only if the e2e, self-test and timing checks show no regression; else turned off with the reason recorded.

**§7 Performance review (AC-10, Q8).** Measured with the existing tools (the pool and playback timing checks, the export timing, `npm run measure:gate`, the print renderer's time per page, the entry and studio chunk sizes): video frame drawing (`renderStack`, `frameStack`, `drawPair`), the decoder pool, the sound mix (`mixWindow`, `gainCurve`), the photo pipeline and the print renderer. Findings in `specs/features/407-code-structure/performance.md`; a change only with ≥ 10 % gain on its path and no loss elsewhere, with before / after numbers.

**§8 Close (AC-9, AC-11).** The full Definition of Done (`npm run check`, `build`, `test:e2e`, `npm test`, `test:mcp`, `check:licenses`), compared with §1's baselines; docs (CLAUDE.md, `specs/testing-strategy.md`, `architecture.md`, `lld.md`, `build.md`, memory); merged into `main`; 207 branches from it.

sections.title: Data Structures & Interfaces
Techniques
sections.markdown:
- **Moves before edits**: `git mv` in its own commit, then fixes, so `git log --follow` keeps each file's history.
- **Warnings first, errors per folder**: the rules land as warnings (the existing code doesn't break the build) and become errors folder by folder, so finished folders can't regress while the rest is cleaned.
- **The standards report** gives every task its before / after numbers (one-letter names, missing JSDoc, long functions, cognitive complexity, casts, React findings, unchecked index errors) for its result note.
- **Renames by meaning, not mechanically**: a name says what the value is in that place (`clip`, `stackItem`, `frameIndex`); the editor's rename (TypeScript language service) for exported names so every importer follows; the type checker and the tests catch slips.
- **Persisted names stay**: fields written to saved projects and agent tool schemas keep their names (renaming them is a format change, out of scope); code destructures them into descriptive locals.
- **Splits by responsibility**: a split moves whole functions with their JSDoc into a module named for its job; no logic changes in the same commit.
- **Type-aware lint cost** is measured (`projectService`, ESLint cache); if `npm run lint` gets much slower, the type-aware rules run in `npm run check` only on changed files plus a full run in the close.

sections.title: Test Approach
sections.markdown:
| AC | Proof | How |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AC-1 | check | `check-structure.mjs` in `npm run check` (fails on a test under `src/`; a planted file proves it) |

sections.title: Decisions for the maintainer (accepted 2026-10-13 with the plan)
sections.markdown:
- **D1 — How tests import the app.** _Chosen:_ a path alias, `@/` → `src/` (`import { valueAt } from '@/engine/keyframes'`), set in Vite and the tsconfigs, for tests only at first. _Alternative:_ relative paths (`../../../src/engine/keyframes`), which break whenever a test or module moves.
- **D2 — After a split.** _Chosen:_ importers are updated to the new modules; no barrel files that re-export the old path. _Alternative:_ keep the old file as a re-export (fewer import changes, but two ways to import the same thing and a module that does nothing).
- **D3 — React Compiler wiring.** _Chosen:_ the Vite React plugin's built-in `compiler` option with `oxc-transform-react` (MIT, no Babel in the build). _Alternative:_ the Babel route (`@rolldown/plugin-babel`, `@babel/core`, `babel-plugin-react-compiler`): the reference implementation, but three more development dependencies and a slower build.

tasks.intro:
**Plan:** `./plan.md`
Legend: `[P]` = can run in parallel with the previous task; 👤 = needs a person. Each task lists files and the proving test.
Behaviour-neutral: each task is moves, renames, splits or type / lint fixes, proven by the existing tests (`npm run check` and `npm run build` green), one commit per task. Tasks run one at a time in the main session.
Unlike phase features (D-033), 407 runs its heavy checks itself (spec Q9): e2e, self-test, MCP and timings run in T001, T013, T014, T043, T056, T060, T061, T071, T072 and T091; nothing is deferred to 290.
When a task is done, record a **Result (YYYY-MM-DD):** note (in single quotes) with `npm run specs -- done 407 Txxx --result '…'`, with the standards report’s before / after numbers for its folder.
